questions.question: Which two attributes are essential for every element?
questions.explanation: src points to the image file, and alt provides the accessible text alternative.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of adding loading="lazy" to an element?
options: It converts the image to grayscale
It delays image loading until it is about to enter the viewport, improving initial load speed
It automatically compresses image resolution on cellular networks
It prevents users from right-clicking to save the image
questions.hint: Think of performance and scroll-based loading.
questions.explanation: loading="lazy" defers downloading off-screen images until the user scrolls near them, speeding up page load.

questions.question: Why should images have explicit width and height attributes specified?
options: To prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) during page rendering
To force the browser to crop the image square
To ensure the image scales to infinity
questions.hint: Reserving layout space prevents jumping content.
questions.explanation: Explicit width and height allow the browser to calculate the aspect ratio and reserve layout space, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).

questions.question: How should a purely decorative background pattern image be tagged for screen readers?
questions.hint: An empty string tells screen readers to ignore it.
questions.explanation: alt="" indicates that the image is decorative, prompting assistive technologies to skip it cleanly.

questions.question: Which element is commonly paired with <figure> to provide an accessible caption for an image?
questions.explanation: <figcaption> is the standard semantic caption element nested directly inside <figure>.
